name: Pskov Russian
notes: Pskov group. This is a WESTERN MIDDLE RUSSIAN АКАЮЩИЙ dialect — 'западных среднерусских акающих говоров' — not the 'mixed North-Central' variety the previous note described without committing to a vowel system. It akajet, so the standard's reduction table applies after hard consonants and is inherited from `ru` unchanged. СИЛЬНОЕ ЯКАНЬЕ is the group's diagnostic and is what this spec adds: 'произношение звука [а] в первом предударном слоге после мягких согласных на месте гласных неверхнего подъёма независимо от гласного, находящегося под ударением'. Independent of the stressed vowel is the whole point — unlike the dissimilative Southern types this one needs no rightward lookahead and encodes exactly, as ⟨я⟩ = [ja] and ⟨е⟩ = [ja]/[a] in the first pretonic syllable only. Later pretonic and posttonic syllables keep the standard readings. ЦОКАНЬЕ: /ч/ and /ц/ merge in [ц], the hard type, and the merger is partial across the group — hence ⟨ч⟩ ranked [ts] over [tɕ] rather than either value alone. Г = plosive: the Pskov group is Middle Russian and sits north of the [ɣ] isogloss. The genitive is therefore the ordinary [v] desinence with standard akanje vowels, opted into from `ru`. Дзеканье (/tʲ/ /dʲ/ with a strong sibilant offglide) and the lisping /sʲ/ /zʲ/ are attested Pskov features that are NOT encoded: they are sub-phonemic qualities the sources consulted describe impressionistically. NEEDS SOURCING.
